questions.prompt: Which is NOT one of the four questions to ask a new table?
choices: What is the mean of every column
questions.explain: A mean is a result, not a check. The fourth question is what the columns are.

questions.prompt: What does value_counts on a category column catch?
choices: The same thing spelled two ways
questions.explain: "Leeds" and "leeds" are two groups to a group-by and one city to a reader.

questions.prompt: Why check min and max on a numeric column?
choices: A sentinel like 999 or a negative age shows up there and not in the mean
questions.explain: The extremes are where impossible values sit. A mean absorbs them and looks plausible.

choices: Before anything is built on the table
questions.explain: Every downstream result built on an unchecked table has to be redone once the table turns out to be wrong.
